prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1157; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision on a city arterial road. The insured vehicle was stopped at a signal when the claimant's vehicle struck it from behind, and the claimant reports neck pain and whiplash symptoms.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene, and the responding officer's account matches the reported sequence of events.

Entry 4: Claimant is represented by counsel; all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office. Requested medical records and an itemized treatment list.

Entry 5: Reviewed scene photographs. They confirm the general location and rear-end contact, but there are no independent witnesses to the impact itself, so the account rests on the parties and the records.

Entry 6: Spoke with the claimant's representative. The claimant has given the same account of the collision in every conversation so far, with no changes to the description of how the impact occurred.

Entry 7: Reviewed the medical file. Treatment followed a typical course for this type of injury and tapered off as the claimant improved. No prior injury to the same body area appears in the records we have.

Entry 8: Consulted the physical damage estimate and the repair photos. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known. Impact severity appears low, and it is not yet clear whether all the repair items came from this collision, so the damage review is continuing.

Entry 9: The claimed injury severity looks high for a low-speed impact of this kind. Referred the file for further medical and engineering review before any settlement position is set.
